questions.question: Why must a model record its dataset version?
options: Because weights and code alone do not identify which examples and features trained it
Because the dataset version determines how many GPU workers the training job requests
Because a model artifact cannot carry any metadata fields beyond its own weight tensors
Because training tables are immutable, so the version is the only input that ever changes

questions.question: What makes a friendly label such as training_v3 insufficient by itself?
options: The label changes automatically whenever any upstream source table is corrected
The label enumerates every source row, which makes it far too large to store
The label can be moved later on unless it resolves to immutable metadata and checksums
The label is minted only at promotion time, so exploratory runs are left unversioned

questions.question: Which item belongs in a training dataset manifest?
options: The display color assigned to the model in the experiment tracking dashboard
The source snapshots, schema fingerprint, feature versions, and label rule
The serving endpoint URL and the replica count the model was deployed with
The number of GPU hours consumed and the queue the training job was sent to

questions.question: Why do training and evaluation data need separate version identities?
options: Because evaluation data carries no labels of its own and therefore cannot be pinned
Because the two sets must contain identical rows for the comparison to be valid
Because a training version cannot be retained once its model has been promoted
Because a correction or contamination removal can change one set without the other

questions.question: How can many dataset versions avoid copying all unchanged bytes?
options: By writing every version into one mutable file that each build job overwrites in place
By discarding source lineage once the dataset version has been checksummed
By sharing immutable snapshot files or content-addressed objects through manifests
By storing only the SQL text and re-running it whenever that version is requested

questions.question: Why must rollback bind model and feature versions together?
options: Because the restored weights can misread the newer feature semantics still being served
Because an older model artifact can no longer be loaded by the current serving runtime
Because feature stores keep no versions, so the model must supply them at load
Because rolling back always requires retraining the model on the older dataset

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: Why is saved SQL insufficient for exact training reproduction?
options: Because query planners rewrite the text, so the plan differs on each run
Because a saved query cannot be re-run without the original credentials and role
Because saved SQL runs against a different warehouse engine after every upgrade
Because the same query reads whatever state the live source tables hold later

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: What should a long training-data build do with source versions?
options: Re-read each source's latest state as every partition of the build is processed
Pin one exact snapshot of every source before any processing begins
Switch to a newer snapshot per partition so late corrections are picked up
Record the wall-clock start time and treat that instant as the source identity

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: Why is a snapshot ID preferable to an as-of timestamp in final lineage?
options: Because a snapshot ID guarantees that all future rows are included in the read
Because a snapshot ID removes the need for any source retention policy at all
Because a snapshot ID names one exact committed state with no clock ambiguity
Because an as-of timestamp changes the result of every query that references it

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: How should an external API input without native snapshots be made reproducible?
options: Capture the response bytes to content-addressed storage with a checksum
Call the live endpoint again at the start of every training epoch for freshness
Record the request URL alone, since the same URL returns the same payload later
Treat the response as stable and note only the date on which it was first read

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: Why can independently taking the latest snapshot of facts and dimensions be inconsistent?
options: Because two tables in one warehouse always share a single global snapshot ID
Because a snapshot stores only data files and never the schema of the table
Because dimension tables are static, so their snapshot never actually advances
Because they can come from different publication cycles rather than one cut

questions.topic: Reproducible Training Data: Snapshots over Live Queries
questions.question: What is the strongest proof of reproducibility?
options: The build SQL parses cleanly against the current warehouse schema definition
A clean rebuild from the pinned lineage reproduces the membership within declared tolerances
A manifest exists and has been checksummed alongside the model registry entry for the run
The dataset carries a stable friendly name that every team resolves identically
